# Commit Messages

Full rules, evidence and examples: `common/writing/commit.md`.

- COMMIT-01 must: Write the subject as `type(scope)?: description` in Conventional Commits form. [tool:conform]
  Good: `feat: add config-sync to gatus`
  Bad: `Add config sync to Gatus.`
- COMMIT-02 must: Use `feat` for any change visible to a user or operator, including enabling, migrating or updating an app in infra repos; `fix` for corrections, `refactor` for restructuring, `perf` for performance, `chore` for maintenance without visible effect, `docs` for docs only, `test` for test-only changes (conform allows it).
  Good: `feat: enable the mail relay` for a new deployed app; `fix: handle empty response`.
  Bad: `chore: enable the mail relay`, or `doc: update setup`.
- COMMIT-04 prefer: Write dependency commits as `chore(deps): update <thing> to vN`; use `feat(deps)` only when the bump changes what ships (upstream provider, major chart).
- COMMIT-05 must: Use no scope except `ci`, `deps` and `release`; they are scopes, never types: write `chore(ci): add workflows`, not `ci: add workflows`. [tool:conform]
  Good: `chore(deps): update nginx to v1.27.3`, `chore(ci): add workflows` and `feat: add retry option`.
  Bad: `feat(client): add retry option` and `ci: add workflows`.
- COMMIT-06 must: Flag a breaking change with a `BREAKING CHANGE: <what breaks>` footer line, not with `!` after the type.
  Good: subject `feat: upgrade to onyx api v6`, footer `BREAKING CHANGE: dropping support for onyx api < v6`.
  Bad: `feat!: upgrade to onyx api v6`
- COMMIT-08 must: Write the description in lowercase imperative mood without a trailing period; keep literal identifiers in their case. [tool:conform]
  Good: `fix: increase trivy operator memory`
- COMMIT-09 prefer: Aim for 3 to 6 words in the description; never exceed 100 characters in the header. [tool:conform]
- COMMIT-10 must: Set the conform header `length` to 100. [tool:conform]
  Good: `.conform.yaml` has `length: 100` under the header rules.
  Bad: `length: 200`.
- COMMIT-11 prefer: Start with a precise verb; use `update` for bumps and `prepare ... to vX` before an unreleased upstream version.
- COMMIT-12 prefer: Name the thing changed instead of echoing the type (`fix: fix X`).
- COMMIT-13 prefer: Prefer `;` over `and` to join two separate changes; `and` inside one noun phrase is fine; use at most two clauses.
- COMMIT-14 prefer: Reference an issue at the end of the subject after a semicolon (`; fix #12`, `; part of #12`); do not use `Closes` footers.
- COMMIT-15 must: Write no prose body; use footers only (`BREAKING CHANGE`, `Release-As: X.Y.Z`).
  Good: `feat: drop the v1 endpoint` with footer `BREAKING CHANGE: v1 endpoint removed`.
  Bad: a three-paragraph body explaining the change.
- COMMIT-17 must: Add no attribution to commits or PR text: no `Co-Authored-By` trailer for agents and no "Generated with" line. Add no `Signed-off-by` either (PR-18 covers PR text).
  Good: `fix: handle empty response` and nothing after the subject.
  Bad: a trailing `Co-Authored-By:` line naming an agent, or `Signed-off-by:`.
- COMMIT-18 lean: Keep AI-written subjects to the owner's average length by dropping the qualifier.
- COMMIT-19 prefer: Let release-please create release commits and notes; pin a manual release with `chore: release X.Y.Z` (no scope; release-please's own commits are `chore(release): release X.Y.Z`) and a `Release-As: X.Y.Z` footer; write no release prose by hand.
- COMMIT-20 prefer: Provide a `.conform.yaml` with the policy `commit` and wire it as a commit-msg pre-commit hook. [tool:conform]

Avoid (AI-Era Artifacts):

- Long subjects that spell out the full behavior.
- Bodies that restate the diff or list files.
- Direct-to-main experiment runs with identical subjects (`update resources (3)` through `(12)`, `play around with homepage` x5); squash or reword when done (PRIN-46).
